messages:
Incident-Bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High error rate from serving-pool-eu-west-2 (GPU nodes). 80% of generation requests returning 5xx in last 2m. Auto-escalation to incidents channel.
Adele Chen: seeing repeated kernel errors in node gpu-eu-12, logs show a GPU kernel abort then container OOM-ish crash, stack traces referencing addr 0x7f3b...
Mike (oncall): paging in. oncall here — what services are affected? any customer-facing 500 spikes?
Adele Chen: yes, traffic spike to /v1/generate for model rdx-3b-quant, ~40% failures for a few customers in eu-west-2. Latency also high when fallbacks trigger.
Nora - runtime: grabbing logs now. likely kernel race on the batch-kernel path. grep for "IllegalAccess" shows repeated lines: 
```
[2027-05-11T14:05:12Z] kernel: GPU0: kernel 0x3f2 failed: illegal address access at pc 0x7f3b24a1
[2027-05-11T14:05:12Z] runtime: trace: kv-cache invalidation race detected
[2027-05-11T14:05:13Z] containerd: container exited with code 137
```
Nora - runtime: also seeing mmapped pointer align warnings in gdb backtraces.
Kai: I'm watching node health metrics — mem usage on GPU is spiking then sudden drop, looks like a kernel-triggered reset. NVML reports GPU_RESET_COUNT++ on gpu-eu-12.
Olivia C: Customer impact: two paying customers in eu-west-2 saw ~30m of increased error rate, some items retried by clients. Support already opened SLA tickets.
Mike (oncall): quick mitigation plan? can we failover traffic to dedicated fallback pool?
Nora - runtime: yes, we have a policy route to cpu-fallback in the same region. I'll trigger routing rule to send new requests for rdx-3b-quant to rdx-3b-cpu-fallback. Expect latency to triple but success rate should recover.
Adele Chen: +1 to reroute. also we should cordon and drain gpu-eu-12 to prevent more resets affecting other pods.
Kai: cordon/drain sequence prepared. Command to cordon: `kubectl cordon gpu-eu-12 -n redwood-serving`. Drain with `kubectl drain gpu-eu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data -n redwood-serving`
Nora - runtime: doing the routing change: `curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/policies/route -d '{"model":"rdx-3b-quant","from":"gpu-pool-eu-west-2","to":"cpu-fallback-eu-west-2","priority":10}'` -> response 202 accepted.
Incident-Bot: Route change applied by Nora - runtime at 14:07:03Z.
Mike (oncall): Kai, proceed with cordon/drain when ready. notify if any node shows >1 reset during drain.
Kai: cordon done. drain in progress. Pod evictions triggered.
Adele Chen: logs from one of the evicted pods show low-level kernel panic before containerd killed it. attaching snippet:
```
[14:06:51Z] runtime: kernel panic in batch-kernel module
[14:06:51Z] driver: illegal device memory access at 0x7f3b24a1 size=256
[14:06:51Z] nvml: GPU 0 reset triggered
```
Adele Chen: I pushed a temporary hotpatch to the serving runtime to avoid the specific batch-kernel code path: set env SERVING_DISABLE_BATCH_KERNEL=1 for the deployment.
Nora - runtime: changed deployment spec for rdx-3b-quant upstream and rolled a canary. Canary on cpu node looks good, no kernel errors.
Olivia C: Support update: notified customers about routing to cpu fallback; provided ETA for mitigation and asked for permission to keep fallback for 2 hours. Customers acknowledged.
Mike (oncall): Good. Next steps: 1) keep fallback routing until node pool is rebuilt; 2) reproduce locally with a stress test to capture a determinist stack trace; 3) next-oncall handoff at 15:00Z if still active. Who will take the handoff?
Adele Chen: I'll stay until 15:00Z, then hand off to Nora if still active. I'm compiling a minimized repro now using the same payload seq that triggered the bug.
Nora - runtime: I'll take over at 15:00Z. I'll also spin up an expanded eviction test in staging to try to hit the reset under instrumented NVPROF.
Incident-Bot: Paging reminder: escalation timer at 14:50Z if error rate not below 1%.
Kai: after drain, gpu-eu-12 shows 3 resets in last 6m. I'm marking it for reprovision: `gcloud compute instances reset gpu-eu-12` then remove from pool and reprovision with fresh image.
Mike (oncall): Approve reprovision. Do we need a kernel or driver rollback?
Nora - runtime: unknown yet. stack traces suggest subtle misalignment when vectorized read crosses a page boundary under certain batch sizes. might be a host kernel-driver interaction, or a JITed kernel bug. We'll collect dpkg/rpm lists and driver versions from the node.
Adele Chen: collected node info: NVIDIA driver 525.60.11, CUDA 12.1, kernel 5.15.0-88, runtime binary commit abc123. Saving to /tmp/incident-1812501120-info.tar.gz
Olivia C: I've updated the incident ticket with customers affected, duration, mitigation steps, and support notes. Ticket ID INC-20270511-442.
Mike (oncall): If we can't repro in staging by 14:50Z and rate remains >1%, we escalate to infra-eng and open a Sev2 bridge. For now we keep CPU routing and reprovision gpu-eu-12.
Nora - runtime: started an instrumented reproduce: script sends 100 concurrent long-context requests with batching enabled and pinned sequence sizes. also enabling extra ulimit and kernel printk for trace.
Adele Chen: repro started in instrumented lab. initial run hit an alignment warning but didn't crash, collecting core and nvcrash logs.
Kai: reprovision in progress: node terminated and new instance provisioning. new node will be gpu-eu-12a.
Incident-Bot: Node reprovision initiated at 14:22:41Z by Kai.
Adele Chen: core dump attached to the ticket (s3://redwood-incidents/1812501120/core-gpu-eu-12-14_06_51.dmp). I've also added the binary and kernel symbols.
Nora - runtime: tracing suggests a race between KV-cache invalidation and batch-kernel compile cache cleanup. adding a conservative lock around compile cache for the canary build.
Mike (oncall): Good mitigation. Keep the CPU fallback until we validate new canary. set rollback window 30m after canary stable.
Olivia C: Sent customer follow-up with summary and mitigation completion ETA.
Adele Chen: canary with the conservative lock deployed to a small subset of GPU nodes (3 pods). monitoring for 10m.
Nora - runtime: after 8m, no illegal-address logs on canary. metrics: error rate from 80% -> 0.5% after routing + canary.
Mike (oncall): who will own postmortem?
Adele Chen: Runtime team will author the postmortem with infra input. I'll draft the timeline and root-cause hypothesis.
Nora - runtime: I'll collect the final traces and driver/kernel diffs and include reproduction steps.
Incident-Bot: Incident state updated: mitigation in place, routing to cpu-fallback, affected node reprovisioned, canary patch deployed. Incident severity lowered to S2 at 14:40:05Z.
Mike (oncall): handing off at 15:00Z to Nora. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
Adele Chen: handing off notes: artifacts, logs, core dump link, canary commit id def456, rollback plan if regressions.
Nora - runtime: taking over. will continue tracking until all nodes on pool have the patch and no regressions for 2h.
Olivia C: support will close customer-facing updates once error rate stable for 1h.
Mike (oncall): closing my page. leaving channel.
Nora - runtime: will file postmortem, label as root cause candidate: kernel-driver alignment bug in batch-kernel path under certain fellowing batch sizes; remediation: conservative lock + upstream bug report to GPU vendor + driver/kernel upgrade testing.
Incident-Bot: Reminder: please add reactions to signal actions (e.g., :white_check_mark: when tasks done).
